speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when you first noticed the painful ulcer on your leg and if it has been getting worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent uveitis, I need to know if you are currently experiencing any gastrointestinal symptoms like abdominal pain or diarrhea. Have you also noticed any new eye redness, pain, or vision changes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of an insect bite followed by a painful, necrotic ulcer with purplish borders in a patient with diabetes is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, potentially triggered by pathergy. I need to rule out infectious causes and vascular insufficiency, so I will request a wound culture and a Doppler ultrasound of the lower extremities. REQUEST TEST: Wound Culture, Doppler Ultrasound Lower Extremities

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Doppler results effectively rule out venous stasis or arterial insufficiency, and the negative culture suggests this is not a primary infection. Given your history of Crohn's disease and the characteristic appearance of the lesion following minor trauma, this clinical picture strongly points to Pyoderma Gangrenosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
